As National Director of Priests for Life, one of America's largest and most visible prolife organizations, and on behalf of the organization, its Board of Directors, and its pastoral team and supporters, I want to express full support of the proposed rule change, namely, to reinstate the full exclusion on abortions and abortion counseling from the medical benefits package offered by the VA. There was no justification to abandon this exclusion. Such abandonment was one of numerous actions by the Biden Administration that were characterized more by a zeal to benefit the abortion industry than to benefit the American people. 
Abortion, as a procedure, is outside the mainstream of medical practice, inasmuch as there is no identifiable medical benefit that derives from the death of an unborn child. Numerous medical professionals testify to this; to name one example, see the American Association of Prolife OB-GYNs (AAPLOG).
Moreover, our ministry oversees the world's largest program for healing those who have had abortions (Rachel's Vineyard), and as we know from the experiences of those who come through our program, many of whom later share their experiences through our Silent No More Awareness Campaign (see AbortionTestimonies.com), abortion does not solve one's problems, but only creates new ones. These problems, which are physiological, emotional, relational and spiritual, are well documented by researchers such as psychiatrist Dr. Martha Shuping, Dr. Priscilla Coleman, Dr. David Reardon, Dr. Theresa Burke, Dr. Phillip Ney, and many others (see LifeAfterAbortion.com). Simply put, our veterans deserve better.
